note: Building wear (DESIGN_IDEAS.md Section 8.13, Dave 4 Nov 2026: go). A piece's condition is worked out lazily from the game time since it was last cared for (placed or repaired, struct 'born'): condition = 1 - (1 - floor) * min(1, t / T) squared. T is in game days (a game day is 3600 real seconds, so 168 game days is one real week), floor is the lowest condition the material can wear to (stone never wears, so it is not listed). kinds maps a structures.json kind to a material; a kind not listed does not wear. Repair (hammer, Repair mode) costs repair_share of the piece's blueprint materials times the condition it lost (rounded up, at least 1 of each), taken from loose items near the piece, then containers within reach, then the pack, and sets the piece back to full condition. A piece above good_condition counts as in good repair.
hammer_reach_note: Master s2.1 (better hammers gain only automatic material-sourcing range and durability), Mission 001 T18: by the hammer tier (Wooden 1 to Steel 5) of the heaviest working hammer on the hotbar, every building distance is multiplied by this: the 12 m stock of a blueprint and a site deposit (pack, ground, own containers and station stores), site_gather_m, the 4 m heavy stock beside a site, and a repair's ground_m and container reach. A wooden hammer keeps today's distances (Dave 10 Nov: 12 m); a steel one reaches 30 m. s5 tuning numbers.
site_gather_note: Dave 10 Nov 2026 ('craft from containers is always a mode people love in other games we are going to build it right in and make it better. it will even pick stuff up from the ground'): the hammer in Repair mode, left click on a blue blueprint site, pulls what it still needs from within site_gather_m of the builder: the pack first, then loose items on the ground and the builder's own containers (not ticked keep out; the crafting rule, craft_stock.gd), nearest first. Always on. Only what is still needed is taken.
